commit_message: feat(app-store): add Proton Calendar integration via CalDAV (closes #5756)
pr_title: feat(app-store): add Proton Calendar integration via CalDAV
pr_body:
## Summary

Adds a Proton Calendar app to the cal.diy app store, fulfilling the long-standing request in #5756. Proton does not publish a public Calendar REST API, but [Proton Bridge](https://proton.me/mail/bridge) exposes the user's encrypted calendars over CalDAV on `127.0.0.1`. This integration reuses the existing CalDAV plumbing (`BaseCalendarService`) and asks the user for the Bridge URL, their Proton email, and the Bridge-generated app password.

## What changed

- New app package `packages/app-store/protoncalendar/` with `_metadata.ts`, `package.json`, `index.ts`, `api/add.ts`, `api/index.ts`, `lib/CalendarService.ts`, `lib/index.ts`, `DESCRIPTION.md`, and `static/icon.svg`.
- `lib/CalendarService.ts` extends `BaseCalendarService` with type `proton_calendar`, mirroring the Apple/CalDAV pattern.
- `api/add.ts` validates the supplied CalDAV credentials by calling `listCalendars()` before persisting them, encrypted, in the `credential` table.
- Setup UI added at `apps/web/components/apps/protoncalendar/Setup.tsx`, registered in `AppSetupPage.tsx`.
- App registered in the generated maps: `apps.metadata.generated.ts`, `apps.server.generated.ts`, `calendar.services.generated.ts`.
- Seed entry added in `scripts/seed-app-store.ts` so the app is created in fresh databases.
- Vitest smoke test for the new `CalendarService` factory + metadata shape.

## Why CalDAV?

Proton intentionally keeps event data end-to-end encrypted and does not expose a public events API. Proton Bridge is the officially supported path for third-party clients; it decrypts the calendar locally and exposes it over CalDAV. Reusing `BaseCalendarService` keeps the integration small and consistent with the existing Apple and generic CalDAV calendars.

Closes #5756.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm install` and `pnpm app-store:build` regenerate the same `apps.*.generated.ts` files (no further diffs).
- [ ] `pnpm test packages/app-store/protoncalendar/lib/CalendarService.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] In a dev environment with Proton Bridge running locally, install the app from the app store, enter the Bridge URL (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:1083`), Proton email, and Bridge app password; verify `listCalendars()` succeeds and a calendar appears under Settings → Calendars.
- [ ] Create a booking that writes to the selected Proton calendar and verify the event appears in Proton Calendar.
notes: Proton has no public Calendar API; the integration relies on Proton Bridge's local CalDAV endpoint (the officially supported path for third-party clients). The CalendarService extends BaseCalendarService and the setup UI asks the user for the Bridge URL, their Proton email, and the Bridge-generated app password. Sandbox has no node_modules, so tests were not executed locally; the maintainer's CI will re-run app-store:build, type-check, and the vitest smoke test on push.
